keyFindings.description: A multi-line value's continuation line that contains '=' and does not start with space/'}'/'-' is parsed as a name (a phantom). The -u on it is a harmless exit-0 no-op and the real entry is removed by its own name, but the phantom is added to `removed` and printed in the boot log line, which promises names-never-values; the count is off by one. Reproduced through the real TmuxRuntime.scrubServerEnvironment on a scratch 3.7c -L server with a fake PEM-shaped value: the log printed the key body's padded last base64 line. bash-exported functions are not a trigger (leading-space body lines, verified via the real binary and via the bash guard-shim `which tmux` resolves to); a raw multi-line secret exported into the daemon env is (only the '='-padded last base64 line of a PEM). Production today: 3 continuation lines in the server table, all canonical function-body lines -> no phantom. Not a regression of the round-2 widening (the old charset matched alphanumeric fragments too); my round-1 note called the phantom a harmless no-op and missed the log. Fix: confirm each candidate with `show-environment <-g|-t s> <name>` (exit 0 present; exit 1 + `unknown variable: <name>` absent -> skip; other refusal throws) before -u and before recording; +1 tmux call per non-allow-listed candidate (66 on production); the probe's stdout is the value and must never be interpolated (failure() is stderr-only). Alternative: parse `show-environment -s` ('"; export NAME;' anchors) — fiddlier escaping; I'd take the probe. Test: the reproduction (continuation line `ZmFr…=`), asserting the phantom is neither -u'd nor returned. Thread: Still open on PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6h3zpW.

'a server without the daemon's session ... is not [fatal] (nothing to scrub or configure — …)' over-generalises: on such a server the global table IS scrubbed (runtime-tmux.ts:453-457, pinned by the 'server without the session' runtime test); only the session table has nothing to scrub or configure. Say 'there'. Fold into the same round; no thread of its own.
